title: FeatureSpec
description: Structured spec of a paper's design feature, emitted by the distiller node. Downstream integration agents implement against this document, so it must be complete enough to implement without the paper.

source.paper_title: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
source.citation: Toru Koizumi, Toshiki Maekawa, Masanari Mizuno, Maru Kuroki, Tomoaki Tsumura, and Ryota Shioya. 2025. RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables. In Proceedings of the 6th Championship Branch Prediction (CBP 2025), June 21, 2025, Tokyo, Japan, pp. 1-6.

summary: The sR component is a statistical corrector (SC) sub-predictor that correlates branch outcomes with recently produced register values. A 65-entry Tomasulo-like tracking table records a 12-bit digest for each logical register as soon as an execution unit produces its value, invalidating the digest after 256 subsequent instructions are decoded to prevent stale data from degrading accuracy. Across 8 banks (each managing 8 or 9 logical registers), usefulness tables (UT) evaluate which available register in each bank correlates best with branch outcomes. For each bank, the digest of the selected register is combined with the PC to index three prediction weight tables (WT). When a bank's usefulness is positive, its weight sum is scaled by 2.5 (otherwise suppressed to 0); the sum across all 8 banks forms the sR partial sum, which is added to the SC linear sum (LSUM). This mechanism is particularly effective immediately after branch mispredictions, when execution units have finished producing values for in-flight instructions before the pipeline restarts.

state.name: reg_status_table
state.organization: Direct-mapped table with 65 entries (one per logical register: 64 architectural INT/FP registers plus 1 condition-code flag register)
state.entry_format: valid: 1 bit, payload: 14 bits (holds either a 14-bit in-flight ROB index when valid=0, or a 12-bit register digest zero-extended when valid=1), decay_ctr: 8 bits (saturating instruction counter tracking up to 256 instructions)
state.indexing: Direct lookup by logical register identifier (register ID in range 0..64)

state.name: sR_UT
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 usefulness tables (UT0, UT1, UT2) of 8 entries each. Each entry stores a vector of 6-bit signed weights corresponding to all logical registers mapped to that bank (Bank 0 has 9 registers; Banks 1-7 have 8 registers each; total 65 registers across banks)
state.entry_format: 6-bit signed saturating counter (-32 to +31) per register. Bank 0 entry: 9 x 6 bits = 54 bits. Banks 1..7 entry: 8 x 6 bits = 48 bits. Total 65 x 6 = 390 bits per table set across all banks.
state.indexing: Skewed PC hash: index = hash_UT(PC, table_id) % 8 (3 bits)

state.name: sR_WT
state.organization: 8 banks; each bank contains 3 prediction weight tables: WT0 (512 entries), WT1 (256 entries), and WT2 (128 entries). Total entries per bank = 896. Total entries across 8 banks = 7168.
state.entry_format: 6-bit signed saturating counter (-32 to +31) per entry
state.indexing: PC and selected register digest: h0 = hash(PC, reg_digest, 0) % 512 (9 bits); h1 = hash(PC, reg_digest, 1) % 256 (8 bits); h2 = hash(PC, reg_digest, 2) % 128 (7 bits)

algorithms.name: compute_register_digest
algorithms.trigger: Execution unit completion: when an instruction finishes execution and produces an architectural register value or flag value
algorithms.notes: Generates a 12-bit digest. Integer registers XOR-fold trailing zeros, leading zeros, and LSBs. FP extracts sign + exponent MSBs aligned at bit 3. Flag registers replicate the 4 bits three times.

algorithms.name: decode_and_decay_update
algorithms.trigger: Instruction decode / rename stage: called for each decoded instruction
algorithms.notes: Decay counter prevents stale data from influencing branch predictions. Once an in-flight instruction re-specifies a destination register, its valid bit is reset and ROB tag is held until completion.

algorithms.name: instruction_complete_update
algorithms.trigger: Instruction execution completion: when an execution unit finishes producing the result value for an instruction
algorithms.notes: Matches ROB index so that older out-of-order completed instructions do not overwrite newer younger dependencies.

algorithms.name: predict
algorithms.notes: The sR partial sum is directly accumulated into LSUM alongside sB, sG, sP, sC, sI, sL, sS, and sT. If max_usefulness <= 0 or no registers are valid in a bank, the bank contributes 0.

algorithms.name: update
algorithms.notes: Random selection of one available register per bank ensures only a single read/write port is needed per table during training.

algorithms.name: squash_recovery
algorithms.notes: Flushing clears pending ROB reservations for squashed speculative instructions while preserving already-completed valid digests, allowing the predictor to exploit completed values immediately upon restart.

host_interfaces.need: register values and execution completion signals from execution units
host_interfaces.description: The predictor requires newly produced 64-bit integer values, floating-point values, and condition-code flags as instructions finish execution to generate and store 12-bit digests.
host_interfaces.fallback: If execution units cannot push values directly to the predictor, forward values at instruction commit or from physical register file writes; in simulators lacking out-of-order execution value forwarding, read speculative architectural register state at branch fetch.

host_interfaces.need: destination logical register ID and ROB tag at decode/rename
host_interfaces.description: When an instruction writing a logical register is decoded, the predictor needs the logical register index (0..64) and the assigned ROB entry index to mark the register as pending execution.
host_interfaces.fallback: If ROB tags are unavailable, clear the valid bit at decode and maintain a 1-bit busy flag cleared at writeback/commit.

host_interfaces.description: A signal or per-instruction decode event to increment the 8-bit decay counter for each register entry, invalidating entries reaching 256 instructions.
host_interfaces.fallback: Increment decay counters on branch instructions only (e.g. invalidating after 32-64 branches) or decrement using cycle-based timers.

host_interfaces.need: branch misprediction resolution and pipeline squash boundary
host_interfaces.description: Identification of squashed instructions upon a branch misprediction to invalidate pending uncompleted ROB dependencies in the register status table.
host_interfaces.fallback: Invalidate all uncompleted (valid=0) entries in the register status table upon any branch misprediction flush.

resource_accounting.storage_breakdown: Prediction weight tables (sR_WT): 8 banks x (512 + 256 + 128 = 896 entries) x 6 bits = 43,008 bits. Usefulness weight tables (sR_UT): 8 banks with 3 tables x 8 entries x 6 bits per register across 65 registers = 65 regs x 24 entries x 6 bits = 9,360 bits. Auxiliary register status tracking table: 65 entries x (valid 1 bit + payload 14 bits + decay_ctr 8 bits = 23 bits) = 1,495 bits. Total = 43,008 + 9,360 + 1,495 = 53,863 bits (6.57 KiB).
resource_accounting.logic_cost_notes: Requires 8 parallel bank evaluations. Within each bank: integer comparator tree across up to 9 registers to find the maximum usefulness; three small SRAM table reads (WT0, WT1, WT2) indexed by hash(PC, digest); a 3-input adder and 2.5x fixed-point multiplier (implemented as (x * 5) >> 1); and an 8-input adder tree across banks. Also requires 12-bit digest generation logic (leading/trailing zero counters and XOR gates) in execution writeback paths.
resource_accounting.budget_donors: At iso-storage, tagged table banks (e.g. shrinking high banks from 25 to 23 banks saves 69,632 bits) or reducing the 128K-entry Bimodal table (e.g. from 128K to 64K entries saves 81,920 bits) can pay for the 53,863 bits of sR.

parameters.name: NUM_BANKS
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales WT size and bank partitioning; storage is proportional to NUM_BANKS

parameters.name: NUM_LOGICAL_REGS
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales UT storage (6 x NUM_LOGICAL_REGS x 24 bits) and status table (23 x NUM_LOGICAL_REGS bits)

parameters.name: UT_ENTRIES
parameters.storage_impact: Directly scales UT size: 6 * NUM_LOGICAL_REGS * 3 * UT_ENTRIES bits

parameters.name: WEIGHT_BITS
parameters.storage_impact: Linearly scales all WT and UT storage

parameters.name: DIGEST_BITS
parameters.storage_impact: Payload field in reg_status_table must be max(14, DIGEST_BITS) bits

unit_tests.name: int_register_digest_xor_folding
unit_tests.given: 64-bit integer register with value 0x0000000000000040. Trailing zeros = 6 (0b000110). Leading zeros = 57 (0b111001). Value[5:0] = 0b000000.
unit_tests.expect: trailing_field = 0b000110; leading_field = 0b111001 << 3 = 0b111001000; lsb_field = 0b000000 << 6 = 0. Digest = 0b000110 ^ 0b111001000 = 0b111001110 (decimal 462). Digest is exactly 12 bits.

unit_tests.name: flag_register_digest_replication
unit_tests.given: Condition code flags register with 4-bit value 0b1011 (decimal 11).
unit_tests.expect: Digest is 4-bit value replicated three times: 0b101110111011 (hex 0xBBB, decimal 3003).

unit_tests.name: fp64_register_digest_extraction
unit_tests.given: 64-bit IEEE-754 double precision float with sign = 1 (bit 63) and exponent MSBs = 0b01111111 (bits 62:55). Bits [63:55] = 0b101111111.
unit_tests.expect: Digest places bits [63:55] at bit positions [11:3], with bits [2:0] set to 0: digest = (0b101111111 << 3) = 0b101111111000 (hex 0xBF8, decimal 3064).

unit_tests.name: stale_digest_decay_invalidation
unit_tests.given: Register R4 receives a valid digest at instruction cycle t. Subsequent instruction stream executes 256 instructions without R4 being updated.
unit_tests.expect: At the 256th instruction decode, R4 decay_ctr saturates/expires and valid bit is cleared to 0. Subsequent branch queries see R4 as unavailable.

unit_tests.name: bank_usefulness_scaling_and_suppression
unit_tests.given: Bank 0 has one available register R0. Sum of UT0, UT1, UT2 for R0 is -3 (non-positive). WT lookup sum (WT0 + WT1 + WT2) is +15. Bank 1 has available register R1 with UT sum +2 (positive) and WT lookup sum +10.
unit_tests.expect: Bank 0 contribution is scaled by x0 (yields 0) due to non-positive usefulness. Bank 1 contribution is scaled by x2.5 (yields +25). Total partial sum from Bank 0 and Bank 1 is +25.

unit_tests.name: training_single_port_random_selection
unit_tests.given: At branch prediction time, Bank 2 had three available registers: R2, R10, R18. At branch commit time, sR update is triggered.
unit_tests.expect: Update algorithm randomly chooses exactly one register among {R2, R10, R18} and updates only that register's entry in UT and corresponding WT weights, requiring only a single write port.

open_questions: U2 (Figure 5 (c) Proposed Register Components): The figure does not explicitly label the control wire selecting between x0 and x2.5 multiplier. Following the panel (a)/(b) usefulness gating analogy and the 'largest / Most useful in this bank' output, the spec assumes that each bank's own usefulness value drives the multiplier (scaling by 2.5 when positive, and suppressing to x0 when non-positive). The alternative reading is a single global static scale of 2.5 with conditional gating, or a global usefulness check.

U3 (Figure 6 (a) INT registers): Count encoding ambiguity. The figure specifies 6-bit fields for leading and trailing zero/one counts, but 64-bit words have up to 64 identical bits (requiring 7 bits). The spec assumes count saturates at 63 (or counts bits matching MSB/LSB excluding the edge bit). Furthermore, the prose states 'zeros (or ones)' without defining whether a mode bit distinguishes zeros from ones, or whether it simply counts leading zeros for non-negative numbers and leading ones for negative numbers (sign-extension count).

U4 (Figure 6 (b) FP registers): Bit-alignment and classification. The right-alignment at digest bit 3 for FP16, FP32, and FP64 is inferred from Figure 6(b)'s drawing and leaves bits [2:0] unused (zero). An alternative reading is that each format's field is right-aligned at bit 0. Additionally, the format classification mechanism ('inspect MSBs') is not specified in the paper for unboxed/NaN-boxed values or general host representations.
